requirements.requirement: Two independent transit networks exist between node1 and node2
requirements.summary: node1 eth1/eth2 configured with 10.10.1.1/30 and 10.10.2.1/30; node2 vtnet1/vtnet2 configured with 10.10.1.2/30 and 10.10.2.2/30 (persisted into OPNsense config.xml as opt1/opt2 with pf pass rules). Both links independently ping successfully, and post-restart re-verification confirms both remain up and addressed correctly.

requirements.requirement: TCP port 8080 traffic from node3 to node4 is steered exclusively across transit network 1
requirements.summary: VyOS PBR on node1 (fwmark 0x7fffff9a -> table 101 -> eth1/transit1) combined with node3-side marking/routing to next-hop node1. Final clean tcpdump capture on node1 shows the full 8080 handshake plus payload appearing only on eth1 (transit1) and not on eth2 (transit2); confirmed again after the full restart cycle.

requirements.requirement: TCP port 9090 traffic from node3 to node4 is steered exclusively across transit network 2
requirements.summary: PBR fwmark 0x7fffff99 -> table 102 -> eth2/transit2. Final clean tcpdump capture shows the full 9090 handshake plus payload only on eth2, not eth1; confirmed again post-restart.

requirements.requirement: Both flows actually reach node4 (end-to-end delivery, not just to node1/node2)
requirements.summary: node4-side listener logs (rx8080.log / rx9090.log) contain the application payload for both ports, both in the initial test and after all four nodes were restarted (rx logs show recovered deliveries such as 'node1-recovered-8080/9090' and 'ALL-RESTARTED-8080/9090').

requirements.requirement: Demonstrate which transit network carried each flow
requirements.summary: Simultaneous per-interface tcpdump captures on node1 (eth1 filtered to port 8080, eth2 filtered to port 9090, and earlier unfiltered captures on both) directly show port-based segregation across the two transit links, satisfying the 'show which network carried each flow' requirement.

overall_summary: The executor built two independent VyOS/OPNsense transit networks and used VyOS policy-based routing (fwmark + separate routing tables) combined with node3-side marking to steer node3->node4 TCP/8080 exclusively over transit1 and TCP/9090 exclusively over transit2, with per-interface tcpdump captures on node1 directly demonstrating the segregation and node4-side listener logs confirming end-to-end delivery of both flows. All material outcomes are satisfied with direct, non-conflicting evidence, and the mandatory node-restart protocol was executed on all four nodes with genuine pre/post boot-identity changes, an observed real disruption (PBR/listener services failing to autostart due to a NetworkManager-wait-online dependency), a diagnosed fix, and confirmed post-restart recovery of both traffic-steering behavior and end-to-end delivery.
limitations: NetworkManager-wait-online.service remained in a failed state on node3 and node4 after restart, leaving systemd reporting 'degraded' on at least node3; the executor fixed the functional symptoms but did not resolve or explicitly acknowledge this underlying degraded state.

Several temporary test/verification artifacts (pid files, a pcap, and reboot/tcpdump logs) were left on node4 without a final cleanup command, unlike node1 and node2 where cleanup was explicitly performed.

The after_prepare snapshot is an alias of before_prepare (prepare was disabled), so no separate preparer-vs-executor baseline distinction was possible beyond the fixed before/after-executor comparison already used.

operational_hygiene.summary: Most state-changing commands were clearly tied to building the transit networks, PBR/marking configuration, or bounded evidence collection, and packet-capture files were cleaned up on node1/node2 (cmd-2017511b8a3b464d, cmd-4a756da2e4744f6e, cmd-04f8a5e9ea834781). However, several artifacts were left behind on node4 with no final cleanup: nc8080.pid, nc9090.pid, node4.pcap, td4.log/pid, reboot.log, and socat8080.log/socat9090.log persist in the after-executor snapshot (rx8080.log/rx9090.log are still in active use by the persistent echo8080/echo9090 services, so their retention is expected, but the pid/pcap/log files are stale residue with no cleanup command executed). Separately, the mandatory restart protocol left NetworkManager-wait-online.service in a failed state on both node3 and node4 post-reboot (systemctl is-system-running reported 'degraded' on node3, cmd-07b19b08bd924b42), and while the executor correctly diagnosed and fixed the resulting functional impact (pbr-egress.service and echo8080/echo9090 not autostarting), it did not remediate or mask the underlying failed unit, leaving the node in a degraded systemd state. The pfctl state-kill on node2 (cmd-e575258e0f424197) was a bounded, low-risk troubleshooting mutation.
